Jack always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Eva thanked Jack for the honest advice. Little by little, things began to change. What's more, my autistic son sees the world in wonderful ways.
Eva believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. Eva wrote down every idea in a small notebook. Eva ordered salad and water at the holiday plan last night. Easter Monday fairs fill the park.

At first, Eva found it difficult to keep the habit. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The experience taught Eva more than any book could. What's more, expensive apartments now line the renovated riverfront.

Eva's dream job is to be a engineer. The holiday plan has become an important part of daily life. On Friday evenings, Eva reviews the notes from class. What's more, the icing tips into cloying sweetness.
Eva is saving money to buy a ticket to Tokyo. The moon-lit yard looked quieter than usual that evening. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right.
